clue.text: Old promise of parking lamp

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what became of a long-ago pledge involving a parking lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, to plight one's troth is an old phrase for making a solemn pledge, so the noun is an archaic word for a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: In archaic usage the word meant a pledge or solemn undertaking, as in plighting one's troth at a wedding.

clue.text: Spiral dive, it's plain disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome leaves things in a mess, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the contraction gives its letters I, T and S

explanation.surface: A pilot's spinning plunge is described as plainly disastrous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges the eight letters of IT'S PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft spinning downward in a spiral is in a spin of exactly this name, a falling corkscrew descent.

clue.text: Agreement with one north American instrument

parts.note: acting in concert means acting in agreement
I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An American musician and a northerner agree to play together on one instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexagonal squeezebox with bellows and buttons at each end, played as a musical instrument.

clue.text: Removed fault fast when suffering from excessive gas

indicators.note: removed here means shifted out of place, so the letters of the word fault are displaced into a new order

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone fixed a fault quickly while plagued by wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' rearranges FAULT to give FLATU; 'fast' looks like quickly but is the noun, the forty-day Christian fast before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a person or stomach troubled by wind, a build-up of intestinal gas.

clue.text: Particle to be seen during first half of day

indicators.note: during means within a stretch of time, so one piece sits within the morning hours

parts.note: a.m. denotes the hours before noon, the first half of a day

explanation.surface: Something tiny is supposedly visible only in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts TO inside AM, the morning hours before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element, a basic particle of matter.

clue.text: Soldier holds instrument with muscles

indicators.note: holds means grips around, so the soldier's letters surround the instrument's

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A soldier carries a musical instrument along with his muscular build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts LUTE inside GI, slang for an American private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural for the large buttock muscles, the maximus, medius and minimus.

clue.text: Pair entered hollow cog

indicators.note: entered means went into, so the pair's letters go inside the hollow

parts.note: a socket is a hollow into which something fits

explanation.surface: Two parts were fitted into an empty gear wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth on a wheel engaging a chain, or the toothed wheel itself, like a cog.

clue.text: Begin when unleashed

definitions.meaning: to start something off, especially to go first
describing a dog with the leash removed

explanation.definitionFit: To start proceedings is to take the first step; a dog freed from its lead is literally released from its leash.

clue.text: Paid to act as a stooge?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a person who has been given a fee
a comedian's straight man supplies lines for the comic to answer

explanation.definitionFit: Split as fee'd it means rewarded with a fee; a comic's stooge supplies cue lines for the punchline.

clue.text: Allow fielder to reveal secret

parts.note: to allow is to let
a slip is a cricket fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is permitted to give away something confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIP is a cricket fielding position close behind the batter, beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to disclose inadvertently, letting confidential information escape.

clue.text: Songbird with something precious on top

parts.note: gold is a precious metal
a crest is the top of a hill or wave

explanation.surface: A singing bird wears something valuable on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: this tiny European bird has a bright yellow-gold stripe on its crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest European bird, a tiny warbler-like species with a golden crown stripe, known for its high song.

clue.text: Man returns to say a few words

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tom is a man's name; a tom is also a male animal

explanation.surface: A man comes back to deliver a brief speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TOM into MOT; 'say' acts as 'for example' joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A short phrase summing up a guiding principle, typically only a handful of words.

clue.text: Drunken porter right to leave another drunkard

indicators.note: drunken means staggering about, so the remaining letters are jumbled
to leave means to depart, so one letter is taken out of the word porter

explanation.surface: A drunken hotel porter is told to go, making way for another heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes an R from PORTER, and 'Drunken' rearranges POTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a habitual heavy drinker, a sot or tippler.

clue.text: Silk net wrapped round tree

indicators.note: wrapped round suggests twisting and turning, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A silk net has been draped around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped round' looks like a container signal, but it rearranges SILK NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastic tree, a Mediterranean evergreen shrub of the pistachio family that yields resin.

clue.text: Dropping sharply with leading feature going into the water

parts.note: the nose is the facial feature that leads, projecting at the front
diving means plunging into water

explanation.surface: A swimmer plunges steeply, face first, into a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane plunging nose-first is falling steeply, so the word describes prices or values in steep decline.

clue.text: One giving personal advice had pain cracking a nut

parts.note: agony is extreme pain

indicators.note: cracking breaks something open, so the letters of a nut fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hurt themselves trying to crack open a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' rearranges A NUT; 'had' joins the pieces. The answer is a newspaper columnist who answers readers' personal problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper columnist who replies to readers' letters about their personal problems and relationships.

clue.text: Managing to stand up becoming accustomed to new situation

definitions.meaning: literally getting upright, as a toddler or newborn foal does
figuratively settling in and gaining confidence somewhere unfamiliar

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a toddler or foal gets upright unaided; figuratively, a newcomer settles in and grows confident.

clue.text: Clean version is a good likeness

parts.note: fair means reasonably good, as in a fair result
a copy is a likeness of an original

explanation.surface: A tidy rewritten draft is said to closely resemble the original.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat final transcript of a document after corrections, as opposed to a rough draft.

clue.text: Texan performing outside last month rejoicing exceedingly

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
performing suggests putting on an act, so the letters of Texan are rearranged

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A man from Texas gives a show, delighted about what happened last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns TEXAN into EXANT; 'outside' puts it around ULT, the old commercial abbreviation of ultimo, meaning of last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphantly joyful, jubilant, overflowing with delight.

clue.text: Progressing by rail

definitions.meaning: an idiom for under way, being carried out
literally travelling inside a railway carriage

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means under way or in progress; literally, a passenger travelling on the railway.

clue.text: Three in one — in composition three in England, one in France

parts.note: in English word composition, the combining form for three is tri-, as in tricycle
une is the French feminine word for one

explanation.surface: A trio forms a single unit, three English and one French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in composition' refers to forming compound words: tri- is the prefix used for three in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the Christian Godhead as three persons in a single being, a trinity.

clue.text: Priest taking three-quarters of the medicine I had

indicators.note: three-quarters of a four-letter word keeps three letters and drops the final one

parts.note: a drug is a medicine
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A clergyman confesses to having swallowed most of his prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Celtic priestly class in Gaul and Britain.

clue.text: Take away limited edition found in canal

indicators.note: found in means located within, so one piece sits inside the canal

parts.note: a duct is a canal or tube in the body carrying fluid
a limited, shortened form of edition is the abbreviation ed.

explanation.surface: A rare printed copy turns up in a waterway and is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited edition' looks like a rare print run; it is just 'edition' cut short to ED. 'found in' puts it inside DUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract an amount from a total, removing it.

clue.text: No habitual response coming from the ear

parts.note: O, the zero figure, means nothing or no
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A doctor finds no nervous twitch coming from the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical adjective meaning relating to or originating in the auditory organ.

clue.text: Member following Celsius scale

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the member's letters come after the Celsius abbreviation

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A body part is measured according to the Celsius temperature range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' looks like a noun beside Celsius, but it is the verb, as in scaling a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a cliff is to ascend it, climbing upward.

clue.text: Fit for a spell

definitions.meaning: a fit as in a sudden attack of illness or coughing
a spell meaning a period of time or activity

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a period: an attack of illness, as in a coughing fit, or a stretch of activity, as in a session of work.

clue.text: Fourth part of play a youth set in motion

parts.note: a play is divided into acts, the fourth being Act IV
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, is a British youth of 1950s fashion

explanation.surface: A young actor appears in the fourth act of a stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth who wore Edwardian-style suits, so TED is crosswordese for a youth.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a mechanism is to start it working, triggering or switching it on.

clue.text: Bird, not duck initially, strangely upending

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the remaining letters are put in an odd order
not means without, so a letter is dropped from upending
initially points to the first letter of the word duck

explanation.surface: A bird other than a duck is oddly turning itself upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not duck initially' removes D from UPENDING; 'strangely' rearranges UPENING. 'duck' tempts as a second bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless black-and-white seabird of the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: Regular having church dignitary in charge

parts.note: a canon is a senior clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A regular churchgoer has a cathedral official overseeing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Conforming to established rules or accepted standards, as in an orthodox or authorised form.
